grammarFocus: 关系从句；指代；可能性表达；复杂句主干辨认。 Teach the new rule in Chinese, then provide at least 8 distinct grammar questions in new sentences. Distinguish a newly taught form from revision. All main reading/listening question prompts and options must be English, with short A0/A1 English prompts. Chinese explanations are allowed. Preserve a coherent new scenario; do not rename an earlier text, reuse its facts or reveal answers in question stems.

title: The Digitisation Dilemma: A Community Weighs the Consequences
instructions: 阅读下面的文章，回答10个问题。文章是关于一个社区团体评估数字化后果的模拟教育材料，并非真实事件。问题类型包括单选、填空、匹配（通过单选实现）和判断正误/未提及。填空题答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。请先通读全文，再作答。语法部分先学习关系从句、指代、可能性表达和复杂句主干辨认的新规则，然后完成8道独立的新句子练习。
passage:
A. The Riverside Community Library, a modest building in the town of Millbrook, had always been a quiet place. But last month, its board of trustees gathered to discuss a proposal that could change everything: a complete digitisation of the library's collection. The plan, which had been drafted by a technology consultant, promised to make thousands of books and documents available online. However, not everyone was convinced. The meeting, which lasted nearly three hours, revealed deep divisions within the community.

B. Margaret Chen, the head librarian, opened the discussion by presenting the benefits. "Digitisation would allow us to preserve fragile manuscripts that are currently too delicate to handle," she explained. "Moreover, it would give residents who cannot easily travel to the library access to our resources." She pointed out that the library's budget, which had been shrinking for years, could be supplemented by grants available for digital projects. Her arguments, which were supported by several board members, seemed persuasive.

C. However, Thomas Reed, a local historian, raised concerns. "The proposal, which focuses only on digitising books, ignores the social function of the library," he argued. "People come here not just to read but to meet and talk. A digital collection cannot replace that." He also worried about the cost, which he believed had been underestimated. "The consultant's estimate, which is based on optimistic assumptions, may not reflect the true expense," he warned. His remarks, which were met with nods from some attendees, highlighted the complexity of the issue.

D. The board also considered the question of who would have access to the digital archive. A subscription model, which would charge users a monthly fee, was proposed as a way to cover costs. But this idea, which many residents opposed, seemed to contradict the library's mission of free public service. "If we charge for access, we might exclude the very people who need it most," said one board member. The discussion, which had become quite heated, showed that the decision would not be easy.

E. In the end, the board decided to form a subcommittee to study the proposal further. The subcommittee, which will include both supporters and critics, is expected to report back in three months. Meanwhile, the library will continue to serve its patrons as it always has. The future of the digitisation project, which remains uncertain, will depend on the subcommittee's findings. For now, the community waits, aware that the choices they make will shape the library for years to come.

questions.prompt: What did the board of trustees meet to discuss?
options: A proposal to digitise the library's collection
A plan to build a new library building
A proposal to reduce the library's opening hours
A plan to hire more librarians
answers: A proposal to digitise the library's collection
questions.explanation: 文章第一段明确指出董事会开会讨论“a proposal that could change everything: a complete digitisation of the library's collection”。
questions.evidence: A. The Riverside Community Library, a modest building in the town of Millbrook, had always been a quiet place. But last month, its board of trustees gathered to discuss a proposal that could change everything: a complete digitisation of the library's collection. The plan, which had been drafted by a technology consultant, promised to make thousands of books and documents available online. However, not everyone was convinced. The meeting, which lasted nearly three hours, revealed deep divisions within the community.

questions.prompt: According to Margaret Chen, what is one benefit of digitisation?
options: It would allow the library to preserve fragile manuscripts.
It would increase the number of printed books.
It would reduce the need for library staff.
It would make the library more popular with children.
answers: It would allow the library to preserve fragile manuscripts.
questions.explanation: Margaret Chen 在第二段提到“Digitisation would allow us to preserve fragile manuscripts that are currently too delicate to handle”。
questions.evidence: Digitisation would allow us to preserve fragile manuscripts that are currently too delicate to handle

questions.prompt: Which distinction underlies Thomas Reed's criticism of the plan's social effects?
options: Access to documents is different from opportunities to meet and talk in a shared place.
Preserving existing manuscripts is the same task as producing new printed books.
A monthly fee is the only way a cultural centre can remain a meeting place.
The price of scanning determines whether residents value social contact.
answers: Access to documents is different from opportunities to meet and talk in a shared place.
questions.explanation: Thomas把读取资料与线下相遇、交谈的社会功能区分开。他没有论证扫描价格决定社交价值，也没有说收费是维持聚会的唯一办法；批评不能简化为“所有数字化都没有价值”。
questions.evidence: C. However, Thomas Reed, a local historian, raised concerns. "The proposal, which focuses only on digitising books, ignores the social function of the library," he argued. "People come here not just to read but to meet and talk. A digital collection cannot replace that."

questions.prompt: Why does the proposed subscription model conflict with the library's stated mission?
options: An access fee could exclude residents despite a mission of free public service.
It prioritises preserving documents over creating a larger physical meeting room.
It postpones a decision until a group reviews the consultant's assumptions.
It gives less-mobile residents digital access while keeping the existing budget unchanged.
answers: An access fee could exclude residents despite a mission of free public service.
questions.explanation: D段把收费模型与免费公共服务使命直接对照，并担忧排除最需要的人。其他选项谈的是保存/社交、后续审查或远程访问等不同议题，没有解释收费与公平访问的冲突。
questions.evidence: A subscription model, which would charge users a monthly fee, was proposed as a way to cover costs. But this idea, which many residents opposed, seemed to contradict the library's mission of free public service. "If we charge for access, we might exclude the very people who need it most," said one board member.

grammar.title: 关系从句、指代、可能性表达与复杂句主干辨认
grammar.explanation: 本课重点学习四个语法点：1) 关系从句：用 which/who/that 等引导，修饰前面的名词。例如：The proposal, which focuses only on digitising books, ignores the social function. 2) 指代：代词如 it, they, this, that 指代前文提到的内容。例如：This idea, which many residents opposed, seemed to contradict... 其中 This idea 指代前文的 subscription model。3) 可能性表达：may, might, could 表示可能性。例如：may not reflect the true expense。4) 复杂句主干辨认：找出主句的主语和谓语，忽略修饰成分。例如：The subcommittee, which will include both supporters and critics, is expected to report back. 主干是 The subcommittee is expected to report back。
grammar.example: The proposal, which focuses only on digitising books, ignores the social function of the library.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun: The book ______ I borrowed from the library is due tomorrow.
options: which
who
where
when
questions.explanation: 先行词是 book（物），关系代词用 which。
questions.evidence: The book which I borrowed from the library is due tomorrow.

questions.prompt: What does 'it' refer to in: 'The library's budget had been shrinking for years, and it could be supplemented by grants.'?
options: The library's budget
The library
The years
The grants
questions.explanation: it 指代前文提到的 the library's budget。
questions.evidence: The library's budget had been shrinking for years, and it could be supplemented by grants.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option to express possibility: The estimate ______ not reflect the true expense.
options: may
must
should
will
questions.explanation: may 表示可能性，符合语境。
questions.evidence: The estimate may not reflect the true expense.

questions.prompt: Identify the main subject–predicate structure after omitting the parenthetical relative clause: 'The steering group, which includes two patient representatives, will publish its report in July.'
options: The steering group will publish its report in July.
which includes two patient representatives
The steering group, which includes two patient representatives
to publish its report in July
answers: The steering group will publish its report in July.
questions.explanation: 逗号之间的which从句补充说明steering group成员。删去该修饰部分后，主语是The steering group，完整谓语为will publish its report in July；其他片段缺主句主语或有限谓语。
questions.evidence: The steering group, which includes two patient representatives, will publish its report in July.

questions.prompt: Combine the sentences using a defining (restrictive) relative clause without a comma: The consultant drafted a plan. The plan promised to make books available online.
options: The consultant drafted a plan which promised to make books available online.
The consultant drafted a plan, which promised to make books available online.
The consultant drafted a plan who promised to make books available online.
The consultant drafted a plan where promised to make books available online.
answers: The consultant drafted a plan which promised to make books available online.
questions.explanation: 题目明确要求不带逗号的限制性关系从句，因此选a plan which promised...。带逗号的非限制性关系从句在合适语境中也合法，但不是本题指定形式；who、where不能在这里作所需的关系代词主语。
questions.evidence: The consultant drafted a plan which promised to make books available online.

questions.prompt: What does 'this idea' refer to in: 'A subscription model was proposed. But this idea seemed to contradict the library's mission.'?
options: A subscription model
The library's mission
Complete digitisation of the collection
The appointment of a consultant
questions.explanation: this idea紧接并指代具体的subscription model（付费订阅方案），不是图书馆使命、更广泛的全部数字化计划或聘任顾问。
questions.evidence: A subscription model was proposed. But this idea seemed to contradict the library's mission.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun: The residents ______ cannot travel easily will benefit from digital access.
options: who
which
where
when
questions.explanation: 先行词 residents 指人，关系代词用 who。
questions.evidence: The residents who cannot travel easily will benefit from digital access.

questions.prompt: Identify the main clause in: 'Although the board discussed the proposal for hours, they decided to form a subcommittee.'
options: they decided to form a subcommittee
Although the board discussed the proposal for hours
the board discussed the proposal
for hours
answers: they decided to form a subcommittee
questions.explanation: 主句是 they decided to form a subcommittee，Although 引导的是让步状语从句。
questions.evidence: Although the board discussed the proposal for hours, they decided to form a subcommittee.
